hints: Notice the neutron is neutral with charge $0$ and, as a baryon, must contain three quarks.
Recall the quark charges in units of $e$: up quark $u$ is $+2/3$ and down quark $d$ is $-1/3$.
Add the three quark charges for each $u$ and $d$ combination and look for the combination that sums to zero.
walkthrough: Identify what is given: a neutron has charge $0$ and baryon number $1$, so it is made of three quarks whose charges must sum to zero.
State the quark charge rule: $Q_u = +2/3e$ and $Q_d = -1/3e$.
Simplify to $Q = (2 - 1 - 1)e/3 = 0$, which matches the neutron charge, while $u u u$ gives $+2e$, $u u d$ gives $+e$ and $d d d$ gives $-e$.

options.A: Three up quarks give total charge $+2e$, not the zero charge of a neutron.
options.B: Two up quarks and one down quark give total charge $+e$, which is the proton composition.
options.C: One up quark and two down quarks give $(+2/3 -1/3 -1/3)e = 0$, the charge of a neutron.
options.D: Three down quarks give total charge $-e$, not the zero charge of a neutron.
